discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 291312
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
912 AM EDT Thu Oct 29 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- 20% to 40% chance of isolated showers this afternoon as a cold
  front moves through. Remaining very warm ahead of the front.

- Not quite as warm this weekend but still above-normal to end
  October.

- 20 to 40% chance of showers on Halloween, mainly west of I- 
  69.

&&

.UPDATE...
Issued at 906 AM EDT Thu Oct 29 2026

Cold front extends from central WI to eastern IA this morning
and is expected to make slow progress through the day. 12Z KILX
sounding shows some improvement in moisture compared to 24 hours
ago, but still a decent amount of dry air in the low levels.
This has resulted in any showers being limited to some
sprinkles. Conditions improve somewhat this afternoon, with pops
on track at this point as isolated to maybe scattered showers
(storm?) develop. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 212 AM EDT Thu Oct 29 2026

High pressure continues to flex its muscle over the eastern CONUS 
early this morning. Water vapor shows fleeting Pacific moisture 
return to a cold front working its way through the Midwest, but 
battling the aformentioned high. Satellite and radar show a broken 
line of showers from central WI (whose population is basking in a 
World Series championship) through eastern Iowa, while a better 
organized area of rain occurs north-northeast of there. Back at 
home, preexisting dry air keeps a majority of the day dry. However, 
there is growing concensus that modest saturation below 16,000 ft 
and adequate upper-level forcing from the right entrance region of a 
departing 500-mb jet will be enough for at least isoalted showers 
along the cold front from west to east after 12pm EDT. Cannot 
completely rule out an isoalted thunderstorm as a thin ribbon of 
instability accompanies the front, per high resolution ensembles. 
Skies quickly clear out behind the front and lows will tumble to 
near 40 by Friday morning. 

The rest of the forecast period is characterized by cooler, but 
still above-normal temperatures, and increasing chances for 
rain. We continue to monitor the 20-40% chance of showers 
Saturday west of I- 69 as a weak shortwave lifts in from the 
Southern Plains. Preceding high pressure, will be fighting to 
keep Halloween dry, yet the rain chance must continue at this 
time. The better surge of moisture arrives in the Sunday-Monday 
time frame as high pressure centers over the Appalachians 
steering Gulf moisture poleward. This area of rain would be 
followed by a mid-latitude cyclone in the Tuesday- Wednesday 
period, bringing mild and breezy conditions ahead of it, rain, 
and then a dose of cooler air. The magnitude of these details 
remain murky owing to the uncertain degree of phasing between a 
subtropical jet moving over the Baja, and a Great Basin trough 
poised to move onshore this weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 607 AM EDT Thu Oct 29 2026

Existing TAFs remain on track at this time. A narrow area of 
MVFR ceilings upstream warrants the continued MVFR mention at 
KSBN. Otherwise, opted to improve visiblilty associated with
-SHRA given the shallow moisture source. Isoalted afternoon
 showers give way to veering surface wind, becoming calm near
 daybreak with decreasing clouds behind the front.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

spc.summary: Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the U.S. through tonight.
spc.text:
SPC AC 291627

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1127 AM CDT Thu Oct 29 2026

   Valid 291630Z - 301200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the U.S. through
   tonight.

   ...Synopsis...
   Water-vapor imagery late this morning indicates a progressive,
   low-amplitude flow pattern over the contiguous U.S.  A cold front
   will push eastward across the Great Lakes with the western portion
   of the front stalling over the central Great Plains and slowly
   advancing northward late tonight.  

   A few afternoon thunderstorms are expected along the front over
   parts of the Great Lakes and Midwest regions, but weak CAPE and
   limited moisture should preclude any severe threat.  Farther
   southwest, a storm or two may develop near the front in the vicinity
   of southern KS.  The weakly forced setup will likely limit storm
   coverage.  Although a strong storm cannot be ruled out, will forego
   introducing hail probabilities this outlook update.  Later tonight,
   weak warm advection will favor elevated buoyancy and the development
   of scattered thunderstorms over northeast KS into the adjacent parts
   of southeast NE/western IA and northwest MO.

   ..Smith/Chalmers.. 10/29/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.summary: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms are possible across portions of southern/central Arizona on Friday. Damaging wind gusts and large hail will be possible with the strongest storms.
spc.text:
SPC AC 290516

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1216 AM CDT Thu Oct 29 2026

   Valid 301200Z - 311200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   ARIZONA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms are possible across portions
   of southern/central Arizona on Friday. Damaging wind gusts and large
   hail will be possible with the strongest storms.

   ...Synopsis...

   A mid/upper shortwave disturbance will migrate through larger-scale
   ridging over the Plains on Friday. This shortwave trough will lift
   slowly northeast from the southern Rockies/Rio Grande vicinity to
   the Mid/Lower MO Valley by early Saturday. Further west, another
   mid/upper trough off the Pacific coast will pivot northeast across
   the Lower CO Valley and Four Corners vicinity. Widespread showers
   and thunderstorm activity are expected with these features, though
   severe thunderstorm potential will be focused across AZ.

   ...AZ...

   Mid/upper south/southwesterly flow around 20-40 kt will overspread
   50s to low 60s F dewpoints Friday morning into the afternoon.
   Diurnal heating may be muted in some locations due to early
   thunderstorm development and cloudiness. Nevertheless, cool
   temperatures aloft (around -12 to -15 C at 500 mb) will support
   500-1250 J/kg MLCAPE. Vertically veering wind profiles, increasing
   in speed in the midlevels, will result in 20-30 kt effective shear
   magnitudes and modestly elongated hodographs. While muted heating
   will limit stronger destabilization, and the expected widespread
   nature of convection may quickly lead to convective overturning, at
   least some risk of severe wind/hail will accompany stronger, better
   organized convection through early evening, particularly across
   southern to central AZ.

   ..Leitman.. 10/29/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 290634

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0134 AM CDT Thu Oct 29 2026

   Valid 311200Z - 011200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected on Saturday.

   ...Synopsis...

   A weak mid/upper shortwave impulse will spread east from the
   central/southern Plains to the Mid/Lower MS Valley on Saturday.
   Modest boundary layer moisture (increasing near the Gulf Coast) and
   cool temperatures aloft (around -10 to -12 C at 500 mb) will support
   sufficient instability for widely scattered showers and
   thunderstorms from OK/TX toward the Lower MS Valley. Overall severe
   thunderstorm potential will remain limited by generally weak flow
   and lack of stronger surface cyclogenesis. Additional thunderstorms
   are possible across portions of the Great Basin as an upper trough
   deepens across the Pacific Northwest and northern Great Basin at the
   same time as a southern stream upper trough approaches the southern
   CA and Baja coasts. Severe thunderstorms are not expected with this
   activity.

   ..Leitman.. 10/29/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
